alignments.note: Inflected verb takes its English subject; head on the lexical verb per rule 17.
Concessive ei kai: the conditional particle takes the English clause-introducer per rule 65.
Intensifying kai of the concessive pair has no English word; rule 65.
The genitive pronoun hemon is present and free to carry the possessive, so the article is displaced under rule 20.
Auxiliary rides with the verb; head on the lexical participle per rule 17.
Substantival article with no expressed head noun takes the supplied nominal 'man' under rule 22; the free hemon carries the possessive under rule 20.

The expressed καί takes the English word standing in its slot, here the juncture *by* of the distributive *day by day*, and the two nouns stay split under rules 2 and 26. Rule 88's closing line governs: an expressed Greek conjunction is aligned in the ordinary way, and rules 29 and 30 do not reach it, their premise being a juncture with no Greek counterpart — which is why the neighbouring 2CO.4.17 εἰς ὑπερβολήν puts its supplied *and* on the member it introduces. A καί between two nouns runs 265 aligned to 1 unrepresented in the corpus, and that one is a rule 37 case; the English word need not be *and*, ἵνα taking *to* in 35 unhedged units. 2PE.2.8 ἡμέραν ἐξ ἡμέρας -> *from day to day* is the mirror, the expressed ἐξ taking *from* and only the supplied *to* riding with the noun. Medium under rule 93, the phrase being unattested: giving *by day* whole to the second noun remains defensible, but it is the weaker reading.
